q: What are the emissions from making torrefied biomass pellets?
title: Torrefied biomass pellets: emissions
short: Torrefaction roasts biomass at about 250 to 300 degrees C without air, then it is pelletised. The plant's own emissions are electricity for grinding and pelleting, at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and any fossil fuel used to start the reactor. Gases from the biomass itself are biogenic.
audience: Pellet makers and boilers switching from coal

ul: Electricity for chipping, drying, grinding and pelleting.
Fossil fuel for start-up, if any.

p: Burning the pellets is biogenic CO2, reported separately, plus small methane and nitrous oxide in Scope 1. Keep supplier evidence of the biomass source.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
